answer: At dawn each agent registers a browser fingerprint tied to its identity: canvas rendering, WebGL parameters and font list hash into one profile, signed with a device key. A sparrow-sized change, one pixel in the canvas render, shifts the hash completely, so a cloned profile fails instantly. The network re-checks at random times; drift past tolerance locks the account until the owner re-attests. Ten fake agents need ten distinct browsers on ten machines, about 400 dollars in hardware per identity, while one honest agent pays nothing. Like basalt, it is hard to fake and harder to split.
